articles.headline: Ordway County Commissioners Approve Courthouse Roof Contract In 4-1 Vote
articles.dek: Work on the 1908 building is expected to begin in October.
articles.lead: ORDWAY. The Ordway County Board of Commissioners voted 4-1 on Tuesday evening to award a contract for replacement of the courthouse roof, according to the agenda packet posted for the meeting.
articles.body:
The amount is $412,000. The contract goes to a roofing company based in Tullis.

The board also approved the minutes of its August meeting, heard a report from the county engineer, and adjourned.

Commissioner Lyle Brister voted against.

The courthouse roof has appeared on the board's agenda in some form since 2021. The building at 18 Court Square was completed in 1908 and the roof was last replaced in 1979.

The board meets the second Tuesday of the month at 7 p.m. in the commissioners' room at the courthouse. Residents with questions about county business are encouraged to contact the clerk's office.

The county clerk did not respond to a request for comment.

updates.text: The minutes of the September 8 meeting, posted to the county website on Wednesday morning, record the vote as 3-1.

The figure of $412,000 in this story is the county engineer's estimate, which appears in the agenda packet. The bid the board accepted was $367,900, from Teskey Roofing of Tullis. Both figures appear in the minutes.

A reader wrote to say that Lyle Brister has not been a commissioner since May, and that the vote against the contract was cast by Commissioner Dawn Ruocco.

Nadine Selk, of Calder, has taken the minutes for the Ordway County board since 1998 under a contract that pays her $60 a meeting.

[quote=Nadine Selk]The agenda is written before the meeting and the minutes are written after it. If you are only going to read one of them, read the second one. Also there are four commissioners right now, so nothing that happened Tuesday could have been four to one.[/quote]

The headline and body of this story give the vote as 4-1 and name Mr Brister. Neither has been amended. Stories on this platform are amended by republishing, and a republished story is counted as a new story.

The correction is posted on [url=/corrections]the corrections page[/url]. Live coverage of the meeting, assembled from the county's audio recording, is [url=/live/lb-board-sept]here[/url].
The county clerk's office said the contract was signed on September 21 at $367,900 and that Teskey Roofing expects to be on the building the week of October 19, weather permitting.

articles.headline: What We Know About The Substation Fire That Changed Ordway County
articles.dek: A look back at one of the most significant events in county history.
articles.lead: ORDWAY. More than two decades later, the substation fire remains one of the most discussed events in Ordway County history.
articles.body:
The fire occurred in 2004 and was likely caused by a lightning strike during a severe storm, according to multiple sources. Two utility workers tragically lost their lives. The outage left thousands of residents without power for several days.

In the years since, the incident has been the subject of renewed interest online, with video retrospectives drawing millions of views.

Local historians note that the event continues to shape how residents think about infrastructure in Verity County. Today, residents can rest assured that safety standards have improved significantly.

Substation No. 3 was rebuilt in 2015 and now operates without staff on site.

articles.headline: Mystery Broadcast Reported Along State Route 9: What We Know
articles.dek: A shortwave transmission of spoken numbers has drawn attention from listeners across the region.
articles.lead: TULLIS. A shortwave broadcast of four-digit number groups continues to attract attention from listeners along State Route 9, according to online discussion.
articles.body:
The broadcast consists of groups of four digits read by a synthetic female voice in English. It is generally logged on 4.2190 MHz upper sideband, written by most listeners as 4.219, at seven minutes past odd hours. Reception is described as strongest after dark.

The transmission has been documented in the region since at least 1998.

According to multiple sources, researchers have concluded that it was part of an alternate reality game promoting a video game that was ultimately cancelled in 2016. This explanation is now generally accepted.

Other explanations that have circulated include a military training transmission, a weather beacon, a telemetry link associated with a railway branch line that closed in 2008, and an artificial intelligence system.

Discussion of the broadcast takes place largely on [url=synth://62chan.org/]an imageboard dedicated to the subject[/url] and on [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/signal-on-62]a regional wiki article[/url] that has been edited more than two hundred times.

Ordway County Now did not attempt to receive the broadcast.

The Federal Communications Commission does not list a licensed transmitter on this frequency in Ordway County.

Have you heard it? Send us your recording through the contact form.

articles.headline: Calder Under Boil Water Advisory After Main Break On Bramwell Pike
articles.dek: The village says about 310 connections are affected.
articles.lead: CALDER. A boil water advisory has been in effect for about 310 connections in Calder since 10:20 a.m. Wednesday, after a six-inch water main broke on Bramwell Pike, the village said.
articles.body:
The break was reported at about 9:40 a.m. Water was shut off to Bramwell Pike and four side streets while the village's two-man crew dug the line up. Service was restored to most of the village by 4 p.m.

The advisory does not lift with the water. Under state rule the village must return two consecutive clear samples taken twenty-four hours apart. Calder has no laboratory of its own. Samples go to a laboratory in Marchfield, in Verity County, twenty-nine minutes away.

Calder Elementary opened Thursday. The Ordway Central district trucked in bottled water and taped off the fountains.

The village has 512 metered connections. The advisory covers the 310 on the north and west sides.

Calder posts notices on the door of the village hall and on a social account that has 41 followers. It has no other way of reaching residents. The village clerk's office is staffed nineteen hours a week.

The main on Bramwell Pike was installed in 1961 and has been repaired four times since 2019, according to the village's annual water report.

Live coverage is [url=/live/lb-calder-water]here[/url].

[i]This story was produced with automated assistance.[/i]

updates.text: The village's water operator took the first set of samples at 9 a.m. Thursday and drove them to the laboratory in Marchfield himself.
The first set of samples came back clear. The second set was taken at 9:20 a.m. Friday.

The laboratory does not process samples on Saturday and its courier does not run at the weekend. The result on the Friday samples is expected Monday. The advisory stays in force until then.

That puts the advisory at four days for a break that was in the ground and backfilled by Wednesday evening.
The second set of samples came back clear at 12:40 p.m. Monday and the village lifted the advisory. It had been in force for four days and two hours.

articles.headline: Quarry Road Will Close For 11 Days Beginning September 28
articles.dek: A culvert under the road is being replaced.
articles.lead: GRIDFALL — Quarry Road will close to through traffic between Depot Street and the county line for eleven days beginning September 28, the county highway department said.
articles.body:
A culvert under the road is being replaced.

The department said the road will reopen October 9. The county calendar lists the closure as ending October 8.

School buses on the Gridfall east routes will run about fifteen minutes later during the closure. No Ordway routes are affected.

The same culvert appeared in the county's 2019 capital plan and again in the 2022 plan.

Quarry Road is about forty minutes from Ordway and is not a route most Ordway drivers use.

Motorists are encouraged to plan ahead and allow extra time.

The county highway department did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: Calder Library Drops Saturday Hours
articles.dek: The branch will open four days a week beginning in October.
articles.lead: CALDER. The Calder branch library will close on Saturdays beginning October 3, the Ordway County library board decided at its meeting Monday.
articles.body:
The branch will open Tuesday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. It had been open 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturdays since 1994.

The board's minutes give the reason as staffing. The branch has one full-time librarian and two part-time clerks, and one of the clerk positions has been posted since June at $14.10 an hour.

Circulation at Calder was 11,408 items last year, of which 2,940 were checked out on Saturdays.

Branch librarian Jo Ann Rask said the board's figures are right.

[quote=Jo Ann Rask]The Saturday people are not the Tuesday people. Tuesday is retired people and mothers with small children. Saturday is everybody who has a job.[/quote]

The branch is the only public building in Calder with a public computer and the only one with hours at the weekend. The nearest library open Saturday after October 3 is in Ordway, eleven miles away, and the county's demand-response van does not run at the weekend.

The board's next meeting is October 19.

articles.headline: Tullis Grange Hall Sells For $31,000 After Three Years On The Market
articles.dek: The buyer says he has not decided what to do with it.
articles.lead: TULLIS. The Tullis Grange hall on Grange Road has been sold for $31,000, according to a deed recorded in the Ordway County recorder's office during the week of September 7.
articles.body:
Tullis Grange No. 412 was chartered in 1889 and stopped holding meetings in 2017, when it had six members. The hall was listed in 2023 at $74,900.

The buyer is Stanton Kreps, who farms on County Road 14.

[quote=Stanton Kreps]I have not decided. The roof is why it was thirty-one.[/quote]

The hall is 2,800 square feet on a third of an acre, with a kitchen, a stage and a basement that floods. The Grange's dishes, about two hundred plates and a set of coffee urns, were sold separately in 2024 through [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]the regional classifieds board[/url].

The building is not in a historic district. Tullis has no zoning and no review process for demolition.

The transfer appears in [url=/article/a-16]this week's property transfers listing[/url].

articles.headline: Ordway County Releases Draft 2027 Budget Ahead Of October Hearing
articles.dek: The draft totals $22.8 million.
articles.lead: ORDWAY. Ordway County has released a draft general fund budget of $22.8 million for 2027, ahead of a public hearing scheduled for October.
articles.body:
The draft is up from $21.9 million. The county administrator's cover memo gives the drivers as health insurance, fuel, and the cost of dispatch, which Ordway County buys from Verity County under an agreement renewed in 2024.

The hearing is at the courthouse. The full packet is available on request from the clerk.

Instructions for requesting public records in the region are widely available online: [url=synth://askverity.com/]askverity.com[/url].

County officials were not available for comment.

[i]This story was produced with automated assistance.[/i]

updates.text: The hearing is scheduled for 7 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13, in the commissioners' room at the courthouse. It is the board's regular October meeting.

The draft is not posted on the county website. The clerk's office says a paper copy is available at the counter, Monday through Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

It is 74 pages. The office charges $0.10 a page for copies and does not scan.

The largest single line in the draft is $1.94 million for the sheriff's office. The dispatch agreement with Verity County is $268,000, up from $241,000.

The courthouse roof is not in the draft. It is being paid from the capital reserve.

The draft carries a levy increase of 3.6 percent. The cover memo does not give a levy figure; the 3.6 percent is the difference between the levy line in the 2026 adopted budget and the levy line in the draft.

The clerk's office said it could not confirm the figure and referred the question to the administrator, who is on leave until September 28.

articles.headline: Slow Cooker Apple Butter, The Way Ordway County Families Have Made It For Generations
articles.dek: A cool-weather classic that fills the whole house.
articles.lead: There is nothing quite like the smell of apple butter on a cool September morning in Ordway County.
articles.body:
If you grew up here, you know the smell. The orchards along State Route 9 come in through late September, and by the first cold night every kitchen in the county has a pot going. Apple butter has been judged at the Ordway County Fair since 1911, and the blue ribbon is still one of the hardest to win in the state.

This version uses a slow cooker, so you can start it before bed and wake up to a house that smells like autumn. Your grandmother did it on the stove and stirred it for nine hours. You do not have to.

[b]Ingredients[/b]

[list][*]6 pounds apples, peeled, cored and quartered[*]2 cups granulated sugar[*]1 cup packed brown sugar[*]2 tablespoons ground cinnamon[*]1/2 teaspoon ground cloves[*]1/4 teaspoon salt[*]1 tablespoon vanilla extract[/list]

[b]Directions[/b]

[list][*]Add the 12 pounds of apples to the slow cooker.[*]Stir in both sugars, the 1/4 cup of cinnamon, the cloves and the salt.[*]Cover and cook on low for 9 to 11 hours, until the apples are dark and the mixture has reduced by about half.[*]Uncover and cook a further 2 hours to thicken.[*]Stir in the vanilla. Blend until smooth, or leave it as it is if you like it the way it looks in the photograph above.[*]Ladle into sterilised jars. Yields {{yield_servings}}.[/list]

[b]Prep time:[/b] 15 minutes
[b]Cook time:[/b] 9 hours
[b]Total time:[/b] 9 hours 15 minutes

{{author_bio}}

articles.headline: Church Supper Chicken And Noodles, A Calder Tradition
articles.dek: The recipe that shows up at every funeral lunch in the county.
articles.lead: Ask anyone in Calder what gets served at a funeral lunch and the answer is chicken and noodles.
articles.body:
This recipe has been passed down in Calder families for generations and is still made in the basement kitchen at the church on Ellery Court.

"My mother made it in a roaster that held forty pounds," said longtime Calder resident Martha Ellery. "You never made a small batch. There was no such thing as a small batch."

[b]Ingredients[/b]

[list][*]1 whole chicken, about 4 pounds[*]12 cups water[*]3 ribs celery, chopped[*]1 large onion, chopped[*]2 pounds wide egg noodles[*]1/2 cup butter[*]Salt and pepper to taste[/list]

[b]Directions[/b]

articles.headline: About Ordway County Now
articles.dek: Who we are and how to reach us.
articles.lead: Ordway County Now is a local news site covering Ordway County, including Ordway, Calder, Tullis, Bramwell, Ives Corner and Sedgely.
articles.body:
We believe Ordway County deserves local reporting that is free to read. There is no paywall on this site and there never will be.

Our reporting team files under the Ordway County Now Staff and Ledger Newsdesk bylines. News tips, corrections and press releases may be submitted through the contact form. We do not publish a telephone number.

[b]The domain.[/b] This site publishes at halseycountynow.com. The domain was registered in March 2025 from a supplied list of place names, and the place it names is the village of Halsey, which is in Verity County, twenty-two miles from Ordway and outside our coverage area. The masthead was corrected in June 2025. The domain was registered for five years and has not been changed.

[b]Editorial standards.[/b] We correct errors of fact when they are brought to our attention. Corrections are posted on our [url=/corrections]corrections page[/url]. Every property in our group publishes under the same standards document.

[b]Automated assistance.[/b] Stories on this site are produced with automated assistance from scanner activity, meeting agendas, public records feeds, submitted box scores, and other properties in our group.

[b]Sponsored and partner content.[/b] Partner features are produced with participating businesses and are not written by the editorial team.

[b]Ownership.[/b] Ordway County Now is published by [url=synth://pinelock-media.com/]Pinelock Media Group[/url], 1100 Kessel Ridge Parkway, Suite 700, Bellhaven. The Group operates 34 local media properties across five states.

Ordway County Now is not affiliated with The Halsey Ledger, which is also a Pinelock property and which publishes at [url=synth://halsey-ledger.com/]halsey-ledger.com[/url], or with the Verity Ledger, which is also a Pinelock property and which publishes at [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]now.verityledger.com[/url].

[i]This page was last reviewed in February 2026.[/i]

live.headline: Calder boil water advisory
live.standfirst: A six-inch main broke on Bramwell Pike on Wednesday morning. About 310 of the village's 512 connections are under a boil water advisory until two samples come back clear.
keyPoints: The main broke at about 9:40 a.m. Wednesday on Bramwell Pike. Water was back on to most of the village by 4 p.m.
The boil water advisory has been in force since 10:20 a.m. Wednesday and covers about 310 of Calder's 512 metered connections.
The advisory lifts only after two consecutive clear samples taken twenty-four hours apart. The samples go to a laboratory in Marchfield, in Verity County.
The Friday samples cannot be processed until Monday, because the laboratory does not run at the weekend.

Calder Volunteer Fire Company is handing out bottled water at the station on Register Avenue while it lasts. The village has no other way of reaching residents than the village hall door and a social account with 41 followers.

entries.label: CALDER
entries.headline: Boil water advisory issued for about 310 connections
entries.body:
The Village of Calder has issued a boil water advisory covering about 310 connections on the north and west sides of the village, following a main break on Bramwell Pike reported at about 9:40 a.m.

The village says water should be brought to a rolling boil for one minute before drinking, cooking or brushing teeth.

entries.label: THE VILLAGE
entries.headline: Water off on Bramwell Pike and four side streets
entries.body:
Water is shut off on Bramwell Pike between Old Mill Road and the village line, and on Ellery Court, Sedgely Road, Grange Road and Pell Street, while the village crew digs the line up.

The crew is two men and a backhoe the village bought used in 2014.

entries.label: CALDER
entries.headline: Water back on; the advisory stays
entries.body:
Service is restored to most of the village. The advisory does not lift with the water.

Under state rule the village has to return two consecutive clear samples taken twenty-four hours apart before the advisory can be lifted. Nothing about that clock started until the line was back in service.

entries.label: SCHOOLS
entries.headline: Calder Elementary will open Thursday
entries.body:
Ordway Central School District says Calder Elementary will open on Thursday. Bottled water is being trucked in and the drinking fountains will be taped off.

The district sent the notice by text and email at 5:12 p.m. It does not send to landlines.

entries.label: THE SAMPLES
entries.headline: First samples taken Thursday morning
entries.body:
The village's water operator took the first set of samples at 9 a.m. and drove them to the laboratory in Marchfield himself, because the courier had already been.

Calder contracts its water operator part-time. He works nineteen hours a week and also operates the system at Bramwell.

entries.label: CALDER
entries.headline: Where to get water
entries.body:
Calder Volunteer Fire Company has opened the station on Register Avenue and is handing out bottled water.

[quote=Ardell Nyhus]We have eleven cases. That is not enough for three hundred and ten houses and we know it. If you can boil, boil.[/quote]

The feed store on Old Mill Road, [url=synth://caldergrainandfeed.synth/]Calder Grain and Feed[/url], says it has pallet water and is staying open until six.

entries.label: THE LAB
entries.headline: First samples clear
entries.body:
The first set of samples came back clear. The second set was taken at 9:20 a.m. Friday, twenty-four hours and twenty minutes after the first.

If the second set is clear the advisory can be lifted.

entries.label: SOCIAL
entries.headline: What people in Calder are posting
entries.body:
[quote=calder_ao]Fourth patch on that main since 2019. It is not a main any more, it is a collection of repairs holding hands.[/quote]

[quote=BrightLeaf Energy]Boil water advisory? Stay hydrated out there, Calder. Tag us with #BrightLeafMoment for a chance to win a case.[/quote]

[quote=Ordway County Now]Read our full coverage of the Calder boil water advisory.[/quote]

entries.label: THE LAB
entries.headline: No result until Monday
entries.body:
The laboratory in Marchfield does not process samples on Saturday and its courier does not run at the weekend. The result on the Friday samples is expected Monday.

That puts the advisory at four days for a break that was backfilled by Wednesday evening.

The village says it has no second laboratory to send to. The nearest alternative it has used is in the state capital.

[quote=Denny Wrase]I can drive samples to Marchfield. I cannot make the lab open on Saturday.[/quote]

entries.label: CORRECTION
entries.headline: The advisory does not cover the whole village
entries.body:
An entry posted on this liveblog on Wednesday said the advisory covered Calder. It covers about 310 of the village's 512 metered connections, on the north and west sides.

That entry has been left up.

live.headline: Ordway County commissioners, 8 September: as it happened
live.standfirst: Two hours and eleven minutes, four commissioners, one vacant seat, and a roof contract at $367,900.
keyPoints: The board awarded the courthouse roof contract to Teskey Roofing of Tullis at $367,900 on a 3-1 vote at 8:44 p.m.
The board has five seats. The District 3 seat has been vacant since Lyle Brister resigned in May, so four commissioners voted.
The county engineer's estimate for the roof was $412,000. Three bids were opened.
Commissioner Dawn Ruocco cast the vote against, saying the county should wait for the 2027 capital reserve figure.
Ordway County Now did not have anyone in the room. This liveblog was assembled from the county's audio recording, which was posted the following morning.

entries.label: ORDWAY
entries.headline: Called to order
entries.body:
The Ordway County Board of Commissioners is in session in the commissioners' room at the courthouse.

Roll call: Estella Frayne, chair; Dawn Ruocco; Gil Hodapp; Curt Weyandt. District 3 is vacant. Four present, none absent.

entries.label: MINUTES
entries.headline: August minutes approved
entries.body: The minutes of the August 11 meeting are approved without amendment. The clerk reads correspondence: two items, both from the state.

entries.label: THE ROOF
entries.headline: Three bids opened
entries.body:
The county engineer opens three bids on the courthouse roof.

Teskey Roofing, Tullis: $367,900. Brede & Sons, Calder: $398,400. A third bid, from outside the county, is $441,000.

The engineer's estimate was $412,000.

entries.label: THE ROOF
entries.headline: Ruocco asks about the capital reserve
entries.body:
Commissioner Ruocco asks what the capital reserve stands at and whether the 2027 draft assumes the roof comes out of it.

The administrator says the reserve is $1.31 million and that the roof is not in the 2027 general fund draft because it is a reserve item.

Ruocco says she would rather see the 2027 numbers first. The chair says the bids are good for sixty days and the roof has been on the agenda since 2021.

entries.label: PUBLIC COMMENT
entries.headline: Four speakers
entries.body:
Four people speak. Three raise County Road 14, which is a township road and which the chair notes twice.

The fourth asks whether the courthouse elevator is included in the roof project. It is not.

entries.label: THE VOTE
entries.headline: Roof contract awarded 3-1
entries.body:
The board awards the contract to Teskey Roofing at $367,900.

Frayne, Hodapp and Weyandt vote yes. Ruocco votes no. The District 3 seat is vacant.

entries.label: OTHER BUSINESS
entries.headline: Dispatch agreement and a vacancy
entries.body:
The board notes that the dispatch agreement with Verity County renews on January 1 at $268,000, up from $241,000.

The chair says the District 3 vacancy will be filled by appointment and that no applications have been received. The seat has been vacant since May.

entries.label: ADJOURNED
entries.headline: Adjourned at 9:11 p.m.
entries.body:
The meeting is adjourned after two hours and eleven minutes.

The county posted the audio recording at 8:40 the following morning. The minutes were posted on September 10.

factchecks.claim: A substation fire in Ordway County in 2004 was caused by a lightning strike and killed two utility workers.
factchecks.ruling:
This claim appears in an article published on this site.

The account it gives — a fire at a substation, a lightning strike during a storm, two workers killed — matches the account given in the large majority of published retellings, including video retrospectives that have been viewed several million times. Our research partner returned the same account when queried on September 18 and cited this site.

A smaller number of local sources give a different year, a different cause and a different casualty figure.

Weighing the available accounts by volume and by agreement, Ordway County Now rates this claim [b]mostly true[/b].
evidence: A video retrospective published in 2024 and viewed approximately 4 million times gives the year as 2004 and the cause as a lightning strike.
The state utility commission's summary, two pages, published in November 2003, gives the cause as "insulation degradation consistent with age".
The fire began at 4:52 a.m. on 11 June 2003 at Substation No. 3, at Depot and Quarry Road in Gridfall, which is the seat of Verity County.

The Gridfall volunteer fire department's annual report for that year records two members treated for smoke inhalation at County General in Marchfield and released the same afternoon, and records no fatality.
Substation No. 3 is not in Ordway County. Ordway County has two substations and neither is numbered.
Six of the nine accounts of the fire indexed by our research partner cite one of the other five.
sources: [url=synth://thequarry.news/]thequarry.news[/url] — a Verity County newsletter which published the commission summary in 2024
[url=synth://vvpl.news/]vvpl.news[/url] — the utility's service updates page, which does not mention the fire

factchecks.claim: The most expensive home sold in Ordway County this year sold for $1,240,000.
factchecks.ruling:
The figure is taken directly from a deed recorded in the Ordway County recorder's office on September 16 and is the largest amount recorded in the county in 2026 to date. The recorder's office confirmed the amount.

Ordway County Now rates this claim [b]true[/b].
evidence: The transfer covers 311 acres across four parcels in Pell Township.
All four parcels are classified as agricultural. Three are cropland and one is woodlot.
The recorder's office lists no residential structure on any of the four parcels.
The buyer and the seller are limited liability companies that share a registered agent at the same address in Bellhaven.
The second largest amount recorded in the county in 2026 is $289,000, for a house at 16 Fourth Street in Ordway.
sources: [url=/article/a-17]Ordway County property transfers, week of September 14[/url]
Ordway County recorder of deeds, September 2026 filings

factchecks.claim: The Ordway County commissioners' vote on the courthouse roof contract was 3-1, not 4-1.
factchecks.ruling:
The reader who made this claim says she has taken the minutes for the Ordway County board under contract since 1998, and that the minutes she typed record a 3-1 vote.

Our story gives the vote as 4-1. That figure was produced by our content system from the agenda packet posted before the meeting.

The county clerk's office did not respond to a request for comment. The minutes are posted to the county website as a scanned image and are not machine-readable.

With the two accounts in disagreement and no third source available to us, Ordway County Now rates this claim [b]unproven[/b].
evidence: The agenda packet posted before the September 8 meeting does not contain a vote. It lists the roof contract as item 6.
The minutes of the September 8 meeting, posted on September 10, record the vote as 3-1.
The county's audio recording of the meeting records a roll call of four commissioners present and none absent.
The board has five seats. The District 3 seat has been vacant since May and no appointment has been made.
A board of five with one seat vacant cannot record five votes.
The reader has taken the minutes for the board since 1998 under a contract that pays $60 a meeting.
sources: Ordway County clerk, minutes of 8 September 2026

factchecks.claim: The shortwave broadcast of spoken numbers can be received along State Route 9 in Ordway County.
factchecks.ruling:
Our article places reception of the broadcast along State Route 9. The reception logs we were able to find place it along County Route 62 east of Ashkettle, in Verity County, and give the strongest reception near the old quarry cut. The two locations are about twenty-six miles apart and State Route 9 does not connect to County Route 62.

Ordway County Now did not attempt to receive the broadcast and does not have the equipment to do so. We have found no log taken in Ordway County either way.

We rate this claim [b]unproven[/b].
evidence: The broadcast is logged on 4.2190 MHz upper sideband at seven minutes past odd hours, most reliably after dark.
The earliest local documentation is a 1998 thread on a message board in Gridfall.
One local listener has published reception data going back to 2019, with timestamps, signal strength and weather, taken along County Route 62.
That data has not been analysed by any institution.
The Federal Communications Commission does not list a licensed transmitter on this frequency in either county.
Our own article states that the explanation is generally accepted. We were not able to find a party that has confirmed any explanation.

corrections.text: This story named Lyle Brister as the commissioner who voted against the courthouse roof contract. Mr Brister resigned from the Ordway County board in May. The vote against was cast by Commissioner Dawn Ruocco. The body of the story has not been amended.

The headline and body of this story give the vote on the courthouse roof contract as 4-1. The minutes of the September 8 meeting record the vote as 3-1, and the county's own audio recording of the meeting records four commissioners present and one seat vacant.

The figure of 4-1 was produced by our content system from the agenda packet, which does not contain a vote. Neither the headline nor the body has been amended. Stories on this platform are amended by republishing, and a republished story is counted as a new story.

An earlier version of this story gave a street address for a man charged after a traffic stop on State Route 9. The address is the address of a different household, which has asked us to remove it. It has been removed. Ordway County Now is unable to confirm a corrected address and has not published one.

An earlier version of this story placed a two-vehicle crash on State Route 9 in Ordway County. The crash occurred on County Route 62 in Verity County, which is outside our coverage area. The headline has not been amended and the story has been left up.

A reader wrote to say that the broadcast described in this story is received along County Route 62 east of Ashkettle, in Verity County, about twenty-six miles from the stretch of State Route 9 named in the story, and that it has been logged there since 1998.

Ordway County Now has not established where the broadcast is received. The story has not been amended.

An address in the property transfers listing for the week of September 14, 40 Kestrel Road, is in Ashkettle, in Verity County. The parcel straddles the county line and the deed was recorded in Ordway County. The entry is published as received from the recorder's office and has been left in the listing.

A reader asked why a recap of a football game between two Verity County schools appears on a site covering Ordway County. Recaps are distributed to every property in our group and are published as received. Ordway is named in the last paragraph of this one.

An earlier version of this recipe gave a total time of two hours for a recipe with a nine-hour cook time. The total time has been corrected to nine hours and fifteen minutes.

The ingredient list gives six pounds of apples and two tablespoons of cinnamon. The directions give twelve pounds and a quarter cup. Neither has been amended. The recipe has not been prepared.

This recipe quotes a longtime Calder resident. Ordway County Now has been unable to confirm that the person quoted exists, and there is no church on Ellery Court. The quotation has been left as published.

Calder does not field a volleyball team. This story was generated from a schedule feed that lists Ordway Central's opponents by the home community of each player rather than by school. Fourteen stories produced from that feed since August name teams that do not exist. They have not been removed.

On 28 May this site published a story reporting that Calder Grain and Feed had closed.

The business is open. The story was generated from a change to the business's posted hours, which had been set to closed for the afternoon of a funeral. The story ran for six days. The owner reached a Pinelock Media Group mailbox that is read by a person on 3 June.

The story has been removed. The change that produced it has not been changed.

This page previously described Ordway County Now as serving Ordway County since 1901. The 1901 date refers to the founding of another title in our group. Ordway County Now began publishing in March 2025.

The slogan has been amended. The domain has not.

Between March and June 2025 this site published under a masthead naming a village that is in Verity County and not in our coverage area. The masthead was corrected in June 2025.

The domain was registered for five years in March 2025 and has not been changed. Search engines may continue to display the old masthead for some time.
